\subsection{0.0.0 (Apr 07, 2026)}
\label{\detokenize{releasenotes:apr-07-2026}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Initial Release}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Documents the proposed solution for the StarSync Network, including architecture,
work packages, and implementation approach for automated repository synchronization
across three machines with GitHub as the central hub.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Executive Summary}
\label{\detokenize{executive_summary:executive-summary}}\label{\detokenize{executive_summary::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This document proposes the detailed approach for delivering the StarSync Network
project. The project addresses the need for automated repository synchronization
between multiple development endpoints (laptop, AWS\sphinxhyphen{}command, AWS\sphinxhyphen{}ai) using GitHub
as the central hub in a star network topology.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The proposed solution implements a cron\sphinxhyphen{}based synchronization script that runs every
5 minutes on each endpoint. The script detects local changes, commits and pushes them
to autosync branches on GitHub, creates pull requests for client review, monitors for
remote changes, and pulls updates automatically. When failures occur, a Hermes agent
is spawned in YOLO mode for autonomous recovery.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The architecture consists of three layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer 1: Endpoints} \textendash{} Each machine runs the sync script via cron

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer 2: GitHub} \textendash{} Acts as the central hub, receiving pushes via autosync
branches and hosting pull requests for review

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer 3: Notifications} \textendash{} Telegram delivers PR URLs to the client for review

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Success will be measured by automatic detection and propagation of changes across
all connected endpoints, with PRs created for review before integration.

\sphinxstepscope

\subsection{Component Design}
\label{\detokenize{proposed_solution:component-design}}

\subsubsection{1. Sync Script (repo\sphinxhyphen{}sync.sh)}
\label{\detokenize{proposed_solution:sync-script-repo-sync-sh}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A bash script deployed on each endpoint that:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads a list of tracked repositories from a config file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each repo:
\sphinxhyphen{} Counts uncommitted changes (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{git status \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}porcelain}})
\sphinxhyphen{} Fetches from origin to check for remote updates
\sphinxhyphen{} If behind origin: stashes local changes, pulls with rebase, restores stash
\sphinxhyphen{} If changes exist and count \textless{}= 500: commits, pushes to an autosync branch
\sphinxhyphen{} Creates a PR via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gh pr create}}
\sphinxhyphen{} Sends a Telegram notification with the PR URL

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns exit code 0 (ok), 1 (failures), or 2 (nothing to do)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{2. Telegram Notification}
\label{\detokenize{proposed_solution:telegram-notification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Upon PR creation, the script uses the Telegram Bot API to send an HTML\sphinxhyphen{}formatted
message containing:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The origin hostname

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Repository name

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Number of files changed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A clickable link to the PR on GitHub

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{3. Agent Fallback (repo\sphinxhyphen{}sync\sphinxhyphen{}agent.sh)}
\label{\detokenize{proposed_solution:agent-fallback-repo-sync-agent-sh}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When the cron detects a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero exit code from the sync script, it invokes
a Hermes agent using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reposync}} profile in YOLO mode with the instruction
to diagnose and resolve the failure. The agent:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads the latest sync log from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/tmp/repo\sphinxhyphen{}sync/}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Attempts automated resolution (abort, reset, conflict handling)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reports results via Telegram

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This enables self\sphinxhyphen{}healing sync operations without human intervention

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{4. Cron Orchestration}
\label{\detokenize{proposed_solution:cron-orchestration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each endpoint has a cron entry running every 5 minutes:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*/5 * * * * /path/to/repo\sphinxhyphen{}sync\sphinxhyphen{}cron.sh \textgreater{}\textgreater{} /tmp/repo\sphinxhyphen{}sync/cron.log 2\textgreater{}\&1 || /path/to/repo\sphinxhyphen{}sync\sphinxhyphen{}agent.sh \textgreater{}\textgreater{} /tmp/repo\sphinxhyphen{}sync/cron.log 2\textgreater{}\&1}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{||}} operator ensures the agent fallback runs only when the sync script
exits with a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero code (failures).


\subsubsection{5. Repository Tracking}
\label{\detokenize{proposed_solution:repository-tracking}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A simple text file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reposync\_repos.txt}}) lists full paths to all tracked
repositories on each endpoint. Lines starting with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#}} are comments, empty
lines are ignored. This file is machine\sphinxhyphen{}specific.


\subsection{Data Flow}
\label{\detokenize{proposed_solution:data-flow}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
User makes changes in a repo on \sphinxstylestrong{laptop}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cron runs (within 5 min): detects changes, commits, pushes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Push creates \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{autosync/laptop/20260407\sphinxhyphen{}XXXXXX}} branch on GitHub

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PR is created targeting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gh\sphinxhyphen{}pages}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Telegram message sent to client with PR URL

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Client reviews at the GitHub PR page and merges

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Next cron cycle on \sphinxstylestrong{aws\sphinxhyphen{}command} pulls the merged changes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All endpoints are now in sync

\end{enumerate}
